answer: The market resists sybils by forcing every new key to lock a bond and finish a serial trail of timestamped, replayable jobs no alias can share. A raven lookout drawn from another operator cohort later checks job graphs and clock jitter; cloned or interleaved traces slash the bond and freeze both keys. Identity is bound to a narrow computational dune—one work-ridge only—so minting a crowd means buying many ridges and surviving a delayed audit. That audit is a short sonnet of countersigned lines, each from a different staked peer, which a script cannot chorus cheaply.
